entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13066"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 5</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Zech.5.1-Zech.5.4">Zec 5:1-4</reference>. Sixth Vision. The Flying Roll. The fraudulent and perjuring transgressors of the law shall be extirpated from Judea.</title> <div sID="gen24549" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13066"/><hi type="bold">1. flying roll--</hi>of papyrus, or dressed skins, used for writing on when paper was not known. It was inscribed with the words of the curse (De 27:15-26; 28:15-68). Being written implied that its contents were beyond all escape or repeal (<reference osisRef="Ezek.2.9">Eze 2:9</reference>). Its "flying" shows that its curses were ready swiftly to visit the transgressors. It was unrolled, or else its dimensions could not have been seen (<reference osisRef="Zech.5.2">Zec 5:2</reference>). Being open to all, none could say in excuse he knew not the law and the curses of disobedience. As the previous visions intimated God's favor in restoring the Jewish state, so this vision announces judgment, intimating that God, notwithstanding His favor, did not approve of their sins. Being written on both sides, "on this and on that side" (<reference osisRef="Zech.5.3">Zec 5:3</reference>) [Vatablus] connects it with the two tables of the law (<reference osisRef="Exod.32.15">Ex 32:15</reference>), and implies its comprehensiveness. One side denounced "him that sweareth falsely (<reference osisRef="Zech.5.4">Zec 5:4</reference>) by God's name," according to the third commandment of the first table, duty to God; the other side denounced theft, according to the eighth commandment, which is in the second table, duty to one's neighbor. <div eID="gen24549" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 5 Zec 5:1-4 . Sixth Vision. The Flying Roll. The fraudulent and perjuring transgressors of the law shall be extirpated from Judea. 1. flying roll-- of papyrus, or dressed skins, used for writing on when paper was not known. It was inscribed with the words of the curse (De 27:15-26; 28:15-68). Being written implied that its contents were beyond all escape or repeal ( Eze 2:9 ). Its "flying" shows that its curses were ready swiftly to visit the transgressors. It was unrolled, or else its dimensions could not have been seen ( Zec 5:2 ). Being open to all, none could say in excuse he knew not the law and the curses of disobedience. As the previous visions intimated God's favor in restoring the Jewish state, so this vision announces judgment, intimating that God, notwithstanding His favor, did not approve of their sins. Being written on both sides, "on this and on that side" ( Zec 5:3 ) [Vatablus] connects it with the two tables of the law ( Ex 32:15 ), and implies its comprehensiveness. One side denounced "him that sweareth falsely ( Zec 5:4 ) by God's name," according to the third commandment of the first table, duty to God; the other side denounced theft, according to the eighth commandment, which is in the second table, duty to one's neighbor.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13067"/><div sID="gen24550" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13067"/><hi type="bold">2. length ... twenty cubits ... breadth ... ten cubits--</hi>thirty feet by fifteen, the dimensions of the temple porch (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.6.3">1Ki 6:3</reference>), where the law was usually read, showing that it was divinely authoritative in the theocracy. The Gentiles are amenable to the curse of the law, as they have its substance, so far as they have not seared and corrupted conscience, written on their hearts (<reference osisRef="Rom.2.15">Ro 2:15</reference>).<div eID="gen24551" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24552" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cut off--</hi>literally, "cleared away."<div eID="gen24552" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24553" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">as on this side ... as on that side--</hi>both sides of the roll [Vatablus]. None can escape, sin where he may: for God from one side to the other shall call all without exception to judgment [Calvin]. God will not spare even "this place," Jerusalem, when it sins [Pembellus]. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13069"/><div sID="gen24555" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13069"/>4. The "theft" immediately meant is similar sacrilege to that complained of in <reference osisRef="Neh.13.10">Ne 13:10</reference>; Mal 3:8. They robbed God by neglecting to give Him His due in building His house, while they built their own houses, forswearing their obligations to Him; therefore, the "houses" they build shall be "consumed" with God's "curse." Probably literal theft and perjury accompanied their virtual theft and perjury as to the temple of God (Mal 3:5). Stealing and perjury go together; for the covetous and fraudulent perjure themselves by God's name without scruple (see <reference osisRef="Prov.30.9">Pr 30:9</reference>).<div eID="gen24555" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24556" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">enter ... the house--</hi>In vain they guard and shut themselves up who incur the curse; it will inevitably enter even when they think themselves most secure.<div eID="gen24556" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24557" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">consume ... timber ... stones--</hi>not leaving a vestige of it. So the "stones" and "timber" of the house of a leper (type of the sinner) were to be utterly removed (<reference osisRef="Lev.14.15">Le 14:15</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="1Kgs.18.38">1Ki 18:38</reference>).<div eID="gen24557" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Zech.5.5-Zech.5.11">Zec 5:5-11</reference>. Seventh Vision. The Woman in the Ephah. Wickedness and idolatry removed from the Holy Land to Babylon, there to mingle with their kindred elements.</title> <div sID="gen24558" type="x-p"/> The ephah is the Hebrew dry measure containing about a bushel, or seven and a half gallons. Alluding to the previous vision as to theft and perjury: the ephah which, by falsification of the measure, they made the instrument of defrauding, shall be made the instrument of their punishment [Grotius]. Compare "this is their resemblance" (<reference osisRef="Zech.5.6">Zec 5:6</reference>), that is, this is a representation of what the Jews have done, and what they shall suffer. Their total dispersion ("the land of Shinar" being the emblem of the various Gentile lands of their present dispersion) is herein fortetold, when the measure (to which the ephah alludes) of their sins should be full. The former vision denounces judgment on individuals; this one, on the whole state: but enigmatically, not to discourage their present building [Pembellus]. Rather, the vision is consolatory after the preceding one [Calvin]. Idolatry and its kindred sins, covetousness and fraud (denounced in the vision of the roll), shall be removed far out of the Holy Land to their own congenial soil, never to return (so <reference osisRef="Zech.3.9">Zec 3:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.27.9">Is 27:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.52.1">52:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.60.21">60:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.50.20">Jr 50:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.13">Zep 3:13</reference>). For more than two thousand years, ever since the Babylonian exile, the Jews have been free from idolatry; but the full accomplishment of the prophecy is yet future, when all sin shall be purged from Israel on their return to Palestine, and conversion to Christ. <div eID="gen24558" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13074"/><div sID="gen24568" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13074"/>9. The agents to carry away the "woman" are, consistently with the image, "women." God makes the wicked themselves the agents of punishing and removing wickedness. "Two" are employed, as one is not enough to carry such a load [Maurer]. Or, the Assyrians and Babylonians, who carried away idolatry in the persons, respectively, of Israel and Judah [Henderson]. As two "anointed ones" (<reference osisRef="Zech.4.14">Zec 4:14</reference>) stand by the Lord as His ministers, so two winged women execute His purpose here in removing the embodiment of "wickedness": answering to the "mystery of iniquity" (the Septuagint here in Zechariah uses the same words as Paul and "the man of sin," whom the Lord shall destroy with the spirit of His mouth and the brightness of His coming, <reference osisRef="2Thess.2.3">2Th 2:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.7.8">7, 8</reference>). Their "wings" express velocity. The "stork" has long and wide wings, for which reason it is specified; also it is a migratory bird. The "wind" helps the rapid motion of the wings. The being "lifted up between heaven and earth" implies open execution of the judgment before the eyes of all. As the "woman" here is removed to Babylon as her own dwelling, so the woman in the Apocalypse of St. John is Babylon (<reference osisRef="Rev.17.3-Rev.17.5">Re 17:3-5</reference>). <div eID="gen24568" type="x-p"/>

"Two" are employed, as one is not enough to carry such a load [Maurer]. Or, the Assyrians and Babylonians, who carried away idolatry in the persons, respectively, of Israel and Judah [Henderson]. As two "anointed ones" ( Zec 4:14 ) stand by the Lord as His ministers, so two winged women execute His purpose here in removing the embodiment of "wickedness": answering to the "mystery of iniquity" (the Septuagint here in Zechariah uses the same words as Paul and "the man of sin," whom the Lord shall destroy with the spirit of His mouth and the brightness of His coming, 2Th 2:3 , 7, 8 ). Their "wings" express velocity. The "stork" has long and wide wings, for which reason it is specified; also it is a migratory bird. The "wind" helps the rapid motion of the wings. The being "lifted up between heaven and earth" implies open execution of the judgment before the eyes of all. As the "woman" here is removed to Babylon as her own dwelling, so the woman in the Apocalypse of St. John is Babylon ( Re 17:3-5 ).
